Is Technology Unnatural-Or Is It 'What Makes Us Human'?

I personally espouse the assertion that technology is as unnatural to humans as termite mounds are unnatural to termites.

I submit that we became cyborgs the moment we picked up a piece of dead matter and deliberately achieved a goal with it at-will that we would not have otherwise been able to accomplish.

I have appended to my body a device that allows me to know exactly how far away tomorrow is from today. It's called a wristwatch.

I have appended to my body several devices that allow me to remain warm and dry in dangerously cold and wet environments. They're called clothes.

"Natural" implies one single thing - natural things occur on their own in nature, or are produced by nature. So with that in mind, anything that exists because of human hands or human creations, is unnatural. Clothing is unnatural, as denim can't be found growing anywhere. Eating utensils are unnatural, as are plates, cars, tooth fillings, stitches, phones, paintings, paint, steel, literally everything that does not occur ON IT'S OWN.

So yeah, tech is unnatural stuff.

My friend, I'm afraid I'll have to humbly disagree with you.

Termite mounds don't exist without termites, nests never build themselves without birds, and if a bee hive is in a tree, it is not because the tree extruded it there out of its bark.

If you look at the universe as a whole, the vast majority of everything is dead gas. A very distant runner up to that is dead dust, and an even smaller proportion still is dead rocks.

Life ITSELF is so astonishingly exceptional that its existence is statistically indistinguishable from not existing at all. Everything we have ever thought of as "Nature", all the animals, plants, microbes, and fungus, even liquid water clouds, rain, rivers, lakes, and seas, and to a lesser extent a warm and thick atmosphere of nitrogen, oxygen, and carbon dioxide, ALL OF THESE THINGS SPITE THE REST OF OUR ENTIRE UNIVERSE AS THUS FAR OBSERVED.

The only thing that hasn't been done on a fundamental level by anything else before in the universe was perhaps the transmutation of Plutonium and the other "trans-uranic" elements. Math suggests that even IF a supernova might spontaneously smash together a few atoms of them they wouldn't even make it through the planetary accretion process before decaying away or fissioning.

TL;DR: What we call "Nature" as we know it is itself actually unnatural. But everything is definitely the result of natural processes... With the exception of maybe plutonium. Maybe.
